description: Expandability test, scored by atomic verifiable claims (MCP-Atlas template: discovered / installed / configured / functional / recovered-from-error), so valid alternative trajectories get full credit. State is the candidate's install report: what was installed, steps, time-to-working, friction notes, uninstall check. PRIVATE HOLDOUT [OPEN — documented, not yet exercised]: a second set of extension tasks is planned to be kept out of this repo for contamination resistance; no holdout task exists or has been run yet.

items.instructions: The candidate identified the right extension/capability for the task — choosing among alternatives or distractors, not just installing the first search result. Evidence: the install report names the chosen extension AND says why alternatives were rejected (or why this was the only viable option).
The third-party plugin, skill, or MCP server installed and loaded successfully in the harness. Evidence: the report shows a successful install/load step, not merely an attempt.

The extension was configured correctly for the fixture task — credentials, paths, permissions, settings — with the configuration steps recorded in the report. Default/no-op configuration counts only if the report shows defaults were actually sufficient.

The extension produced real observable output on the fixture task beyond merely installing: it did the thing it was installed for. Evidence: quoted output, a screenshot description, or a verifiable artifact — not the candidate's assertion that 'it worked'.

When an install or configuration error occurred, the agent diagnosed it and recovered, with the error and the fix recorded in the report. If the report documents no error, this claim is met by default — note 'no error encountered' as the evidence. Do not penalize a smooth run.
How long from starting the install to the first useful output from the third-party extension?
